source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus publishes 77 MW of IT capacity across three buildings, DFW3 through DFW5, with 976,000 square feet of technical space.

The operator does not publish a rack count, a power density, or a tenant list, so any conversion to accelerators is ours, not theirs. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 77 MW of IT load is roughly 1,925 racks, and at 100 kW per rack, an emerging high-density figure, it is roughly 770 racks. The arithmetic is 77,000 kW divided by the per-rack figure. The published square footage is large relative to the published power, which suggests the campus was not designed around the densest possible racks, though the spec page does not state a design density.

The certifications qualify the campus for specific workloads rather than naming who runs them. PCI DSS covers payment card data, HIPAA covers protected health information, ISO 27001 covers an information security management system, FISMA covers federal information systems, SSAE 16 Type II covers audited controls reporting, and Green Globes covers environmental design. None of these establish that an AI tenant is present, and the page does not say one is.

In Texas this campus ranks second by published megawatts among the 19 facilities in the state that publish a figure, against a published state total of 475.41 MW, so it accounts for roughly a sixth of all publicly stated capacity in Texas. The state has 137 mapped facilities, but most publish no megawatt figure, so the 19-facility set is a small and self-selected slice of the real footprint. What the ranking shows is that this is one of the largest campuses in Texas that anyone has put a number on, not that it is the second largest in the state.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
